title: A Witness for the Parish
premise: Edmund Amberdale, a meticulous night-shift dispatcher who has quietly solved three cold cases from her switchboard, is stunned when a drowned woman is pulled from the canal wearing clothes lifted from Edmund's own closet. As police circle her as a suspect, Edmund discovers the victim was a former parish choirgirl who had been living under a stolen identity — Edmund's own childhood name. Following a coded ledger hidden in the parish donation records, Edmund uncovers a decades-old trafficking ring protected by the town's most beloved families, and realizes the killer is silencing everyone who remembers the summer of 1998. In the climax, Edmund baits the killer with a fake ledger page, survives an attack in the church crypt, and exposes the ring — but chooses to keep one name out of the record: her own.
about_author: Juniper Fairweather is a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade transcribing other people's secrets before turning them into fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people whose careful lives are cracked open by the past, and lives near a canal she refuses to swim in.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet Edmund on a rain-slicked night shift, closing her latest cold case by phone, establishing her pride in control and her carefully curated anonymity. A strange call comes in — a woman whispering a name Edmund hasn't heard since childhood. The emotional beat is unease beneath routine: the past tapping on the switchboard.

chapters.title: Clothes That Weren't Given
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The drowned woman is identified, wearing Edmund's own clothes, and Detective Inspector Halloway interviews her at the scene. Edmund recognizes the victim's face from an old parish photograph. The beat is violated privacy — someone has studied Edmund closely enough to become her, and the police now study her too.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Pew Books
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Searching her late mother's things, Edmund finds a parish donation ledger with columns of figures that don't add up — coded entries spanning 1998. She realizes the victim, 'Marian Voss,' had been investigating it. The beat is reluctant curiosity hardening into resolve: Edmund takes the case she can't refuse.

chapters.title: Marian
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: flashbacks from Marian Voss's final week, interwoven with Edmund tracing her rented room. Marian was a witness from the old parish, hiding under a false identity, one step ahead of someone patient. The beat is grief for a stranger who was a mirror — Marian's fear becomes Edmund's inheritance.

chapters.title: The Summer of '98
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund interviews aging parishioners and finds a pattern: four girls left town that summer, three dead since, all under new names. Her own childhood name appears in the ledger. The beat is dread — Edmund wasn't spared from the ring's attention as a child; she was simply never found.

chapters.title: Halloway's Suspect
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Halloway's investigation narrows on Edmund's motiveless connection to the victim, while Edmund realizes the ledger's final entries were updated last month — by someone still alive. A break-in at her flat, nothing stolen but one photograph. The beat is the walls closing in from both sides.

chapters.title: The Benefactor
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The coded figures trace to the parish restoration fund and its charming chairman, Aldous Grebe, whose family bankrolled the town for generations. Grebe offers Edmund a job, a warning, and a memory of her mother all at once. The beat is seduction and menace in a single handshake.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Marian's POV, final entries of her hidden journal, recovered by Edmund. Marian confesses she traded her testimony in '98 for a new life, and returned only to make amends. Edmund confronts the theme head-on: she too survived by forgetting. The beat is devastating recognition — the price of survival was paid by the girls who couldn't run.

chapters.title: The Crypt
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund plants a forged ledger page naming the last living witness and waits in the church crypt at night. The killer comes — not Grebe, but his quiet archivist, the man who kept the records and the names for thirty years. A brutal chase through the crypt ends with Halloway's arrival. The beat is terror transmuted into trap.

chapters.title: A Witness for the Parish
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The archivist confesses; Grebe's empire cracks in the morning papers. Testifying at the inquest, Edmund gives the court everything except the name in the ledger that is hers — choosing, this once, what memory to keep and what to bury. The beat is bittersweet closure: the case closed, the self finally claimed.
